package_info.package_manager: N/A (injected JavaScript via third-party services or direct site compromise)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects any version of compromised scripts or sites)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire injected JavaScript package is malicious because it is designed to surreptitiously capture sensitive payment and personal information from e-commerce website users during checkout, exfiltrating this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure without user or merchant consent.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into e-commerce site pages or third-party JavaScript libraries (e.g., advertising scripts, live chat, customer rating features)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form's submit event, collects sensitive payment and personal data from form fields, and sends this data via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in credential and payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating sensitive data to an external, non-merchant domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or the merchant's own backend, not to unknown third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to payment gateways or for analytics, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: JavaScript event listeners on payment forms
Network requests to untrusted or hardcoded external domains
Collection of sensitive fields (card number, CVV, etc.)

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to e-commerce site or third-party JavaScript provider via vulnerability, credential stuffing, or social engineering.
Malicious JavaScript is injected into the website or third-party script loaded by multiple e-commerce sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming code in user browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits payment information during checkout, the malicious code captures form data and exfiltrates it to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into payment or checkout form events
Outbound network requests from client-side code to untrusted or previously unseen domains during checkout
Collection of sensitive fields (credit card, CVV, billing address) by scripts not belonging to payment processors
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in third-party JavaScript libraries (advertising, chat, rating scripts)
New or modified inline scripts on checkout/payment pages
Obfuscated or minified code with network request logic
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor
Frequent small POST requests during checkout to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized or unexpected JavaScript changes on payment pages, especially scripts that access form fields and make outbound network requests. Use file integrity monitoring on web assets, scan for new or modified third-party scripts, and analyze network traffic from client browsers for suspicious POST requests to unknown domains during checkout. Employ vulnerability scanning and penetration testing to identify and remediate points of injection.
